svg.text: How an Agent Actually Runs: The Core Loop That Repeats Until a Deterministic Gate Exits
Steps 2-5 iterate; Step 1 feeds context in; Step 5 is the only place the loop may end — the same gate exists in ADK, LangGraph, CrewAI, and OpenHands.
• LLM never decides when to exit;
• Every tool call writes a WAL
Each turn plans 1 action, executes 1 scoped MCP call, checkpoints state, and tests the exit gate.
Gemini or Gemma 3 decides tool vs. reply
Output grounding check, OpenTelemetry trace (Cloud Trace /
Langfuse), cost audit, verified answer with receipt.
GOOGLE: Cloud Trace + Model Armor • OSS: OpenTelemetry + Langfuse + Receipt SHA
WHAT IS ALLOWED TO END THE LOOP (STEP 5 GATE) — GOOGLE + OPEN-SOURCE KNOBS
Verification hook returns exit_code == 0 (pytest, schema, or policy
check) — the LLM saying 'done' is never sufficient.
max_steps = 15: ADK RunConfig • LangGraph recursion_limit • CrewAI
max_cost_usd = 0.25 per task via Cloud Billing budgets or a LiteLLM
If sha256(tool + args) fails twice in a 5-turn window (Firestore or
Redis ZADD window), the 3rd attempt is blocked and a strategy shift
Tool result + state are written to Firestore or PostgreSQL
(LangGraph PostgresSaver / Temporal) so a crash resumes at step N
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
Sources: Prashant Rathi (POST-08) • Rakesh Gohel controls • LangGraph recursion_limit • OpenHands max_iterations
